Posted by Hanno Böck on Nov 25 Hello, 
 
Lately, I'm observing that Ubuntu's response to severe security flaws 
is concerning. 
 
On November 16th, details about a remote memory corruption called 
NoisyTCP (CVE-2026-99288) in the Linux kernel's TCP stack were 
published:  https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/11/15/2  
Today, nine days later, Ubuntu still has not published a fix yet: 
 https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-99288  
Other distros had a fix already...

items.title: 354 dark web vendors and buyers arrested in Europol-coordinated global crackdown
items.summary: Europol, in collaboration with law enforcement agencies from 14 countries across the globe, have successfully identified vendors and buyers from major dark marketplaces as part of Operation TorNado, a coordinated international effort targeting cybercrime, drug trafficking, and firearms offences. The operation, which spanned from May 2025 to October 2026, resulted in 354 arrests and hundreds of house searches worldwide.

items.title: Five TEFAF robbery suspects added to EU Most Wanted
items.summary: As of 29 October 2026, five new fugitives, four men and one woman, have been added to the EU Most Wanted list. According to the Limburg Public Prosecutor's Office (Openbaar Ministerie) and the Dutch Police (Politie), all five suspects are involved in the European Fine Art Fair (TEFAF) robbery that took place on 28 June 2022 in Maastricht, the Netherlands.
